title: Sectionwise flat module presheaves give finite-limit-preserving tensor functors
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, and let $P$ be a presheaf of $R$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Assume that $P(V)$ is a flat $R(V)$-module for every object $V$: tensoring with $P(V)$ preserves injective maps of $R(V)$-modules. Define $T_P$ on presheaves of $R$-modules by $T_P(A)=A\otimes_{p,R}P$ and $T_P(f)=f\otimes1$, using the presheaf tensor product [def-pur-presheaf-tensor-product]. Then $T_P$ preserves finite limits. More explicitly, for every presheaf-module morphism $f:A\to B$, the canonical morphism $(\ker f)\otimes_{p,R}P\to\ker(f\otimes1)$ is an isomorphism compatible with the kernel inclusions. For every finite family $(A_i)_{i\in I}$, the canonical morphism $(\prod_i A_i)\otimes_{p,R}P\to\prod_i(A_i\otimes_{p,R}P)$ induced by the projections is an isomorphism, including $I=\varnothing$. Both comparisons are morphisms of presheaves with the given semilinear restriction maps.

source.place: Tag 03ES (lemma-flatness-presheaves), with the finite-limit formulation of presheaf flatness in Tag 03ER (definition-flat), (1); explicit kernel and finite-product comparisons extracted from the sectionwise proof.

proof.text: Write $r_A:A(V)\to A(W)$ and $r_P:P(V)\to P(W)$ for restriction along $u:W\to V$. By [def-pur-presheaf-tensor-product], restriction on $T_P(A)$ sends $a\otimes p$ to $r_A(a)\otimes r_P(p)$. Semilinearity over $r_R:R(V)\to R(W)$ respects the balancing relation: both restrictions of $(ca)\otimes p=a\otimes(cp)$ equal $r_R(c)r_A(a)\otimes r_P(p)$. For a module-presheaf morphism $h:A\to B$, the maps $h_V\otimes1$ commute with these restrictions, since $r_Bh_V=h_Wr_A$. The identities for composition, identity arrows and addition hold on pure tensors, which generate each tensor module. Thus the stated $T_P$ is an additive functor.

source.place: Tag 03ES (lemma-flatness-presheaves), expanding its proof; Section 03EK (section-tensor-product) and Section 03CS (section-presheaves-modules).

proof.text: For $f:A\to B$, put $K(V)=\{a\in A(V):f_V(a)=0\}$, with the induced $R(V)$-module structure. Naturality of $f$ restricts $r_A$ to semilinear maps $K(V)\to K(W)$; the presheaf laws are inherited from $A$. A morphism $h:H\to A$ with $fh=0$ has the unique factorization $h_V(x)\mapsto h_V(x)\in K(V)$ at every $V$. These factorizations are linear and commute with restrictions, so $K$ with its inclusion $i:K\to A$ is the categorical kernel.

source.place: Tag 03ES (lemma-flatness-presheaves), expanding its proof; Section 03EK (section-tensor-product) and Section 03CS (section-presheaves-modules).

proof.text: For a finite family $(A_i)_{i\in I}$, form $Q(V)=\prod_{i\in I}A_i(V)$ with coordinatewise operations and restrictions. The projections are module-presheaf morphisms, and a family of morphisms $h_i:H\to A_i$ has the unique factorization $x\mapsto(h_i(x))_i$ into $Q$, which is linear and natural coordinatewise. Hence $Q$ is the categorical product. For $I=\varnothing$ it is the zero presheaf, with its unique maps. The same construction applies to the family $(T_P(A_i))_i$.

source.place: Tag 03ES (lemma-flatness-presheaves), expanding its proof; Section 03EK (section-tensor-product) and Section 03CS (section-presheaves-modules).

proof.text: Fix $V$. The section sequence $0\to K(V)\xrightarrow{i_V}A(V)\xrightarrow{f_V}B(V)$ is exact by step 2. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] with the commutative ring $R(V)$ and its flat module $P(V)$, using precisely the sectionwise flatness hypothesis. It gives an exact sequence $0\to K(V)\otimes_{R(V)}P(V)\xrightarrow{i_V\otimes1}A(V)\otimes_{R(V)}P(V)\xrightarrow{f_V\otimes1}B(V)\otimes_{R(V)}P(V)$. Consequently $i_V\otimes1$ has zero kernel and image $\ker(f_V\otimes1)$. Its corestriction $\alpha_V:K(V)\otimes_{R(V)}P(V)\to\ker(f_V\otimes1)$ is therefore an $R(V)$-linear isomorphism; it is characterized by $j_V\alpha_V=i_V\otimes1$, where $j_V$ is the target kernel inclusion.

source.place: Tag 00HD (lemma-flat), tensor exactness; applied sectionwise as in sites-modules.tex Tag 03ES (lemma-flatness-presheaves).

proof.text: The maps $\alpha_V$ commute with restrictions. Indeed, for $u:W\to V$ and $k\otimes p\in K(V)\otimes_{R(V)}P(V)$, the images of the two possible composites under $j_W$ both equal $r_A(i_V(k))\otimes r_P(p)=i_W(r_K(k))\otimes r_P(p)$. The injectivity of $j_W$ and generation by pure tensors give equality of these semilinear maps on every element. Thus $\alpha$ is the canonical morphism of presheaves $T_P(K)\to\ker T_P(f)$, and $j\alpha=T_P(i)$. Its component inverses are linear and natural: the identity $r\alpha_V=\alpha_Wr$ implies $r\alpha_V^{-1}=\alpha_W^{-1}r$ with the source and target restrictions in their respective positions. Hence $\alpha$ is an isomorphism of module presheaves compatible with the inclusions.

source.place: Tag 03ES (lemma-flatness-presheaves), expanding its proof; Section 03EK (section-tensor-product) and Section 03CS (section-presheaves-modules).

proof.text: For the products from step 3, the tensor-projection morphisms give $\beta:T_P(Q)\to\prod_iT_P(A_i)$. At $V$ it sends $(a_i)_i\otimes p$ to $(a_i\otimes p)_i$. Choose a bijection of the finite set $I$ with $\{1,\ldots,t\}$, the same bijection for all $V$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-finite-product] over $R(V)$, with factors $A_i(V)$ and $N=P(V)$: $\beta_V$ is an isomorphism, also for $t=0$. Along $u:W\to V$ both orders of restriction and $\beta$ send $(a_i)_i\otimes p$ to $(r_{A_i}(a_i)\otimes r_P(p))_i$. Thus $\beta$ is natural, and its component inverses are natural by the inverse identity used in step 5. It is the canonical presheaf isomorphism induced by the projections. For the empty family both sides are zero; alternatively, every pure tensor in $0\otimes P(V)$ is $0\otimes p=0$.

source.place: Tag 03ES (lemma-flatness-presheaves), expanding its proof; Section 03EK (section-tensor-product) and Section 03CS (section-presheaves-modules).

proof.text: Finally let $D:J\to\mathrm{PMod}(R)$ be any finite diagram. Put $Q_0=\prod_{i\in\operatorname{Ob}J}D_i$, $Q_1=\prod_{a:i\to j\in\operatorname{Mor}J}D_j$, and define $\delta:Q_0\to Q_1$ by $\operatorname{pr}_a\delta=D(a)\operatorname{pr}_i-\operatorname{pr}_j$. Then $L=\ker\delta$, with the restricted projections, is a limit: a map $H\to Q_0$ is a tuple $(h_i)$, and $\delta(h_i)=0$ is exactly the cone equations $D(a)h_i=h_j$; step 2 gives their unique factorization through $L$. All these maps are module-presheaf morphisms. Under the product comparisons of step 6, $T_P(\delta)$ is the corresponding difference map for $T_P D$: its $a$-component on a pure tensor is $(D(a)x_i-x_j)\otimes p=D(a)x_i\otimes p-x_j\otimes p$. This uses the additivity from step 1. The kernel comparison of steps 4–5 now identifies $T_P(L)$ with the kernel of that difference map, compatibly with every projection, hence with the limiting cone of $T_PD$. This includes the empty diagram by step 6. Thus the canonical comparisons for every finite diagram are isomorphisms, which is preservation of finite limits.
